# OpenAI telemetry and semantic-conventions manual

Generated by **OpenTelemetry Weaver 0.28.0** using `.j2` templates.
Evidence snapshot: **2026-10-18**. Regenerate with `mise exec -- scripts/generate-reference.sh`.

The native event, metric and span definitions below come directly from the same YAML registry used for generated
bindings. Supporting desktop analytics declarations and public cloud schemas are retained as evidence catalogs;
they are not silently converted into native OTLP exports. qyl's development adapter contract is identified separately.
The registry schema URL identifies the catalog definition, not a schema URL claimed by the native producer.
Experimental and deprecated entries remain visible. The boundary is pinned client source, the inspected installed
bundle and published schemas; private backend fields and account-specific delivery remain outside that evidence.

## Native source coverage

| Catalog | Audited names | Registered definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime event names | 46 | 46 |
| Runtime metric names | 256 | 256 |
| Runtime span names | 236 | 237: the shared exec-server request name has distinct client and server definitions |

`otel.kind` and `otel.name` are tracing bridge controls, not invented ordinary OTLP attributes. Literal source span
names and dynamically overridden exported names are distinguished in the source annotations. Empty metric units
mean that the native instrument omits unit metadata; semantic value units remain documented separately.

## qyl's cross-producer adapter contract

This defines the broad identity, lifecycle and state model used to interpret native observations. It does not claim
that OpenAI emits qyl-prefixed records. The production implementation must demonstrate deduplication, correct
unit conversion, identity continuity and actual collector ingestion before claiming operational support.

### entity.qyl.agent.operation

One logical operation tracked across its observed lifecycle.

| Property | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | `entity` |
| Stability | development |
| Signal collection | recommended |
| name | `qyl.agent.operation` |
| Registry schema | https://qyl.at/schemas/15.0.3 |
| Source | `registry/qyl/agent-observability.yaml` |

The operation identifier is stable across delivery retries. Parent and turn attributes describe relationships;
they are not unsupported entity-relationship declarations. State changes never alter identity.


| Attribute | Type | Requirement / role | Sampling relevant | Stability | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gen_ai.tool.call.id` | string | recommended; descriptive | Not applicable | development | The tool call identifier supplied by the model or provider. |
| `qyl.agent.operation.id` | string | identity (no requirement level) | Not applicable | development | Stable identifier for one observed logical operation. |
| `qyl.agent.operation.name` | enum | recommended; descriptive | Not applicable | development | Bounded operation category used for cross-producer comparisons. |
| `qyl.agent.operation.state` | enum | recommended; descriptive | Not applicable | development | Last established lifecycle state of an operation. |
| `qyl.agent.parent.operation.id` | string | recommended; descriptive | Not applicable | development | Identifier of the directly enclosing observed operation. |
| `qyl.agent.turn.id` | string | recommended; descriptive | Not applicable | development | Native turn or prompt identifier scoped to its provider and conversation. |

#### Attribute details: `gen_ai.tool.call.id`

This attribute SHOULD be set to the identifier received from the model or provider
if and only if one was supplied.


Examples: `["call_mszuSIzqtI65i1wAUOE8w5H4"]`.

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.operation.id`

An adapter MUST reuse this identifier across the operation's lifecycle and retries of record delivery.
Use a source-provided invocation ID scoped by product, workspace and session, with one documented
mapping shared by observers. A per-event record ID, fresh random value or timestamp is not an operation
identity. When the source does not establish an operation identity, retain the source record without
inventing an operation entity or lifecycle. This high-cardinality identifier belongs on events and spans,
not metrics. Reconcile equivalent observations across sources before counting the same operation twice.


Examples: `["openai:workspace-7:thread-42:call-9"]`.

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.operation.name`

A model retry remains a separate request attempt within its enclosing turn. Record daily aggregates as aggregates, not fabricated operations.

| Member | Wire value | Stability | Meaning / deprecation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `turn` | `turn` | development | One agent turn. |
| `model_request` | `model_request` | development | One model request attempt. |
| `tool` | `tool` | development | One tool invocation. |
| `approval` | `approval` | development | One approval decision cycle. |
| `task` | `task` | development | One explicitly identified background or cloud task. |

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.operation.state`

Missing telemetry does not imply completion or failure. Approval denial, process exit, tool completion
and turn completion are different facts. Map a source outcome only within the operation it describes.
This is descriptive entity state and MUST NOT be part of entity identity.


| Member | Wire value | Stability | Meaning / deprecation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `queued` | `queued` | development | Accepted and waiting to start. |
| `running` | `running` | development | Execution has started. |
| `waiting` | `waiting` | development | Explicitly waiting for an external decision or dependency. |
| `completed` | `completed` | development | Completed successfully according to the source. |
| `failed` | `failed` | development | Failed according to the source. |
| `cancelled` | `cancelled` | development | Explicitly cancelled or interrupted. |
| `unknown` | `unknown` | development | Current state cannot be established from available observations. |

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.parent.operation.id`

Record only when the source establishes the parent. Temporal proximity or matching model names do not establish ancestry.

Examples: `["openai:workspace-7:thread-42:turn-3"]`.

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.turn.id`

Codex turn.id and Claude prompt.id can populate this field when their source contracts identify the
request being observed. Do not equate a conversation, a model request and a turn. Turn IDs can be absent.


Examples: `["turn-3"]`.


### entity.qyl.agent.session

A conversation within the namespace of its originating product.

| Property | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | `entity` |
| Stability | development |
| Signal collection | recommended |
| name | `qyl.agent.session` |
| Registry schema | https://qyl.at/schemas/15.0.3 |
| Source | `registry/qyl/agent-observability.yaml` |

Product plus conversation ID identify this entity. Adapters MUST additionally scope tenant-local IDs
before assigning gen_ai.conversation.id. Model provider is descriptive and may change during a session.
These are identity fields; Weaver 0.28.0 does not attach requirement_level to materialized identity.


| Attribute | Type | Requirement / role | Sampling relevant | Stability | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gen_ai.conversation.id` | string | identity (no requirement level) | Not applicable | development | The unique identifier for a conversation (session, thread), used to store and correlate messages within this conversation. |
| `gen_ai.provider.name` | enum | recommended; descriptive | Not applicable | development | The Generative AI provider as identified by the client or server instrumentation. |
| `qyl.agent.product` | enum | identity (no requirement level) | Not applicable | development | Product responsible for the observed activity. |
| `service.name` | string | recommended; descriptive | Not applicable | stable | Logical name of the service.  |

#### Attribute details: `gen_ai.conversation.id`

Instrumentations SHOULD populate conversation id when they have an identifier
for the conversation readily available for a given operation, for example:

- when the client framework being instrumented manages conversation history
(see [LlamaIndex chat store](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/module_guides/storing/chat_stores/),
[LangChain `session_id`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-core/runnables/history/RunnableWithMessageHistory),
and [Google ADK sessions](https://adk.dev/sessions/session))
- when instrumenting GenAI client libraries that maintain a conversation on the backend
(see [AWS Bedrock agent sessions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-session-state.html),
[OpenAI Assistant threads](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/threads))

When no identifier for the conversation is available, instrumentations SHOULD NOT
populate conversation id. For example, a new UUID, a trace identifier, or a hash
of request content SHOULD NOT be used as a fallback value.

Application developers that manage conversation history MAY add conversation id to GenAI and other
spans or logs using custom span or log record processors or hooks provided by instrumentation
libraries.


Examples: `["conv_5j66UpCpwteGg4YSxUnt7lPY"]`.

#### Attribute details: `gen_ai.provider.name`

Semantic conventions for individual GenAI operations SHOULD clarify which
kinds of providers (e.g. inference, embeddings, retrieval, memory, hosted
agent providers) apply when it is not clear from context.

The attribute SHOULD be set based on the instrumentation's best knowledge
and may differ from the actual upstream provider. For example, a client SDK
may be configured against a proxy or hosting platform that transparently
relays requests to a different provider.

The `gen_ai.provider.name` attribute acts as a discriminator that
identifies the GenAI telemetry format flavor specific to that provider
within GenAI semantic conventions.
It SHOULD be set consistently with provider-specific attributes and signals.
For example, GenAI spans, metrics, and events related to AWS Bedrock
should have the `gen_ai.provider.name` set to `aws.bedrock` and include
applicable `aws.bedrock.*` attributes and are not expected to include
`openai.*` attributes.


| Member | Wire value | Stability | Meaning / deprecation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `openai` | `openai` | development | [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) |
| `gcp.gen_ai` | `gcp.gen_ai` | development | Any Google generative AI endpoint |
| `gcp.vertex_ai` | `gcp.vertex_ai` | development | [Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai) |
| `gcp.gemini` | `gcp.gemini` | development | [Gemini](https://cloud.google.com/products/gemini) |
| `anthropic` | `anthropic` | development | [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/) |
| `cohere` | `cohere` | development | [Cohere](https://cohere.com/) |
| `azure.ai.inference` | `azure.ai.inference` | development | Azure AI Inference |
| `azure.ai.openai` | `azure.ai.openai` | development | [Azure OpenAI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/overview) |
| `ibm.watsonx.ai` | `ibm.watsonx.ai` | development | [IBM Watsonx AI](https://www.ibm.com/products/watsonx-ai) |
| `aws.bedrock` | `aws.bedrock` | development | [AWS Bedrock](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock) |
| `perplexity` | `perplexity` | development | [Perplexity](https://www.perplexity.ai/) |
| `x_ai` | `x_ai` | development | [xAI](https://x.ai/) |
| `deepseek` | `deepseek` | development | [DeepSeek](https://www.deepseek.com/) |
| `groq` | `groq` | development | [Groq](https://groq.com/) |
| `mistral` | `mistral` | development | [Mistral](https://mistral.ai/) |
| `moonshot_ai` | `moonshot_ai` | development | [Moonshot AI](https://www.moonshot.ai/) |

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.product`

This is product attribution, not the underlying model provider. For example, Codex may use a configured non-OpenAI model provider.

| Member | Wire value | Stability | Meaning / deprecation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `codex` | `codex` | development | Codex execution. |
| `chatgpt` | `chatgpt` | development | ChatGPT activity. |
| `claude_code` | `claude_code` | development | Claude Code execution. |
| `cowork` | `cowork` | development | Cowork execution. |
| `claude` | `claude` | development | Other documented Claude activity. |

#### Attribute details: `service.name`

MUST be the same for all instances of horizontally scaled services. If the value was not specified, SDKs MUST fallback to `unknown_service:` concatenated with the process executable name, e.g. `unknown_service:bash`. If the process executable name is not available, the value MUST be set to `unknown_service`.
The process executable name is the name of the process executable, the same value as described by the [`process.executable.name`](process.md) resource attribute.


Examples: `["shoppingcart"]`.

### event.qyl.agent.operation.state_changed

A source-established change in one operation's lifecycle state.

| Property | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | `event` |
| Stability | development |
| Signal collection | recommended |
| name | `qyl.agent.operation.state_changed` |
| Registry schema | https://qyl.at/schemas/15.0.3 |
| Source | `registry/qyl/agent-observability.yaml` |

Emit after deduplication. Preserve source time and original record identity when available. Correlate by
explicit operation, turn, tool-call or trace identities; never by proximity alone. Late and out-of-order
observations must not silently rewind a terminal operation. Record uncertainty instead of guessing.
This development adapter contract does not claim that OpenAI or Anthropic emits this qyl event natively.


| Attribute | Type | Requirement / role | Sampling relevant | Stability | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `qyl.agent.operation.id` | string | required | Not applicable | development | Stable identifier for one observed logical operation. |
| `qyl.agent.operation.name` | enum | required | Not applicable | development | Bounded operation category used for cross-producer comparisons. |
| `qyl.agent.operation.state` | enum | required | Not applicable | development | Last established lifecycle state of an operation. |
| `qyl.agent.product` | enum | required | Not applicable | development | Product responsible for the observed activity. |
| `qyl.agent.record.id` | string | recommended | Not applicable | development | Stable identity of the original source record within its source stream. |
| `qyl.agent.record.observed_at` | string | recommended | Not applicable | development | UTC ISO 8601 time at which the adapter observed the source record. |
| `qyl.agent.record.payload` | any | opt_in | Not applicable | development | Optional original source record retained for explicitly enabled diagnostics. |
| `qyl.agent.source` | enum | required | Not applicable | development | Collection boundary from which an observation was obtained. |

Deduplicate at-least-once delivery using source stream/workspace plus this value. OpenAI compliance event_id is suitable in its documented stream scope; a timestamp alone is not.

Examples: `["event-123"]`.

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.record.observed_at`

Keep the original event time on the event timestamp. This field measures collection delay and does not replace source time.

Examples: `["2026-10-18T06:00:00.000Z"]`.

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.record.payload`

May contain conversation content, commands, personal identifiers and secrets. Omit by default. Apply
redaction, access controls and a configured byte limit before export. Preserve a separate external
reference when truncation would make the record unusable. Never place this value on a metric.


Attribute annotations:

```json
{
  "type": {
    "json_schema": {
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "value": {
    "unbounded_size": true
  }
}
```

### metric.qyl.agent.operation.duration

Duration of completed observed agent operations.

| Property | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | `metric` |
| Stability | development |
| Signal collection | recommended |
| metric_name | `qyl.agent.operation.duration` |
| instrument | `histogram` |
| unit | `s` |
| Registry schema | https://qyl.at/schemas/15.0.3 |
| Source | `registry/qyl/agent-observability.yaml` |

Record once per deduplicated completed operation with a known duration. Convert native milliseconds to
seconds explicitly. A source duration with a different boundary is a different measurement and must not
be merged. Dimensions are bounded categories; exclude conversation, operation, turn, tool-call and user IDs.

### metric.qyl.agent.operation.status

Number of currently tracked operations in each lifecycle state.

| Property | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | `metric` |
| Stability | development |
| Signal collection | recommended |
| metric_name | `qyl.agent.operation.status` |
| instrument | `updowncounter` |
| unit | `1` |
| Registry schema | https://qyl.at/schemas/15.0.3 |
| Source | `registry/qyl/agent-observability.yaml` |

Each tracked operation contributes 1 to its current state and 0 to every other member of the closed state
set. Transition by subtracting 1 from the previous state and adding 1 to the next. Aggregate by bounded
dimensions, without operation IDs. Publish zero for empty states. The observer must document its tracked
population and terminal-record retention, remove contributions when records expire, and rebuild the current
population after restart before reporting it. This is current state, not a cumulative transition count.
A historical event stream without sufficient state reconstruction cannot honestly emit this metric.

#### Attribute details: `qyl.agent.operation.id`

An adapter MUST reuse this identifier across the operation's lifecycle and retries of record delivery.
Use a source-provided invocation ID scoped by product, workspace and session, with one documented
mapping shared by observers. A per-event record ID, fresh random value or timestamp is not an operation
identity. When the source does not establish an operation identity, retain the source record without
inventing an operation entity or lifecycle. This high-cardinality identifier belongs on events and spans,
not metrics. Reconcile equivalent observations across sources before counting the same operation twice.


Examples: `["openai:workspace-7:thread-42:call-9"]`.

### span.qyl.agent.operation.internal

One observed agent operation, with explicitly established start and end boundaries.

| Property | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | `span` |
| Stability | development |
| Signal collection | recommended |
| span_kind | `internal` |
| Registry schema | https://qyl.at/schemas/15.0.3 |
| Source | `registry/qyl/agent-observability.yaml` |

Start when the source establishes that this operation begins; end on its matching terminal observation.
A retry of a model request is a child attempt, not a new whole turn. Do not synthesize a span from a daily
analytics row or a lone completion record with unknown start time. Preserve native spans when available
instead of creating duplicate wrapper spans. The low-cardinality span name is `agent {qyl.agent.operation.name}`.
Set Error status only for an established operation failure, with error.type. Expected cancellation or denied
approval is not automatically an error. Leave successful status Unset. Do not put identifiers in span names.
Product, operation category and established identity are available at start; state, duration and error facts
become available at completion and cannot be assumed present for head sampling.


| Attribute | Type | Requirement / role | Sampling relevant | Stability | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `error.type` | enum | {"conditionally_required":"If the observed operation failed."} | false | stable | Describes a class of error the operation ended with.  |
| `gen_ai.conversation.id` | string | recommended | false | development | The unique identifier for a conversation (session, thread), used to store and correlate messages within this conversation. |
| `gen_ai.tool.call.id` | string | recommended | false | development | The tool call identifier supplied by the model or provider. |
| `qyl.agent.operation.id` | string | required | false | development | Stable identifier for one observed logical operation. |
| `qyl.agent.operation.name` | enum | required | false | development | Bounded operation category used for cross-producer comparisons. |
| `qyl.agent.operation.state` | enum | recommended | false | development | Last established lifecycle state of an operation. |
| `qyl.agent.parent.operation.id` | string | recommended | false | development | Identifier of the directly enclosing observed operation. |
| `qyl.agent.product` | enum | required | false | development | Product responsible for the observed activity. |
| `qyl.agent.source` | enum | required | false | development | Collection boundary from which an observation was obtained. |
| `qyl.agent.turn.id` | string | recommended | false | development | Native turn or prompt identifier scoped to its provider and conversation. |

#### Attribute details: `error.type`

The `error.type` SHOULD be predictable, and SHOULD have low cardinality.

When `error.type` is set to a type (e.g., an exception type), its
canonical class name identifying the type within the artifact SHOULD be used.

If the recorded error type is a wrapper that is not meaningful for
failure classification, instrumentation MAY use the type of the inner
error instead. For example, in Go, errors created with `fmt.Errorf`
using `%w` MAY be unwrapped when the wrapper type does not help
classify the failure.

Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.

The cardinality of `error.type` within one instrumentation library SHOULD be low.
Telemetry consumers that aggregate data from multiple instrumentation libraries and applications
should be prepared for `error.type` to have high cardinality at query time when no
additional filters are applied.

If the operation has completed successfully, instrumentations SHOULD NOT set `error.type`.

If a specific domain defines its own set of error identifiers (such as HTTP or RPC status codes),
it's RECOMMENDED to:

- Use a domain-specific attribute
- Set `error.type` to capture all errors, regardless of whether they are defined within the domain-specific set or not.


Examples: `["timeout","java.net.UnknownHostException","server_certificate_invalid","500"]`.

| Member | Wire value | Stability | Meaning / deprecation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `other` | `_OTHER` | stable | A fallback error value to be used when the instrumentation doesn't define a custom value.  |

#### Attribute details: `gen_ai.conversation.id`

Instrumentations SHOULD populate conversation id when they have an identifier
for the conversation readily available for a given operation, for example:

- when the client framework being instrumented manages conversation history
(see [LlamaIndex chat store](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/module_guides/storing/chat_stores/),
[LangChain `session_id`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-core/runnables/history/RunnableWithMessageHistory),
and [Google ADK sessions](https://adk.dev/sessions/session))
- when instrumenting GenAI client libraries that maintain a conversation on the backend
(see [AWS Bedrock agent sessions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-session-state.html),
[OpenAI Assistant threads](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/threads))

When no identifier for the conversation is available, instrumentations SHOULD NOT
populate conversation id. For example, a new UUID, a trace identifier, or a hash
of request content SHOULD NOT be used as a fallback value.

Application developers that manage conversation history MAY add conversation id to GenAI and other
spans or logs using custom span or log record processors or hooks provided by instrumentation
libraries.


Examples: `["conv_5j66UpCpwteGg4YSxUnt7lPY"]`.

#### Attribute details: `gen_ai.tool.call.id`

This attribute SHOULD be set to the identifier received from the model or provider
if and only if one was supplied.


Examples: `["call_mszuSIzqtI65i1wAUOE8w5H4"]`.

## Reading this manual

There are several different contracts, even when the same product name appears on all of them:

| Layer | What it represents | Where you obtain it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime OTel logs | Individual operations and their diagnostic details | An explicitly configured OTLP log collector |
| Runtime OTel spans and span events | Operation timing, parent/child relationships, and selected events | An explicitly configured OTLP trace collector |
| Runtime metrics | Aggregated counters, gauges and distributions | Configured OTLP metrics exporter; a filtered subset can go to OpenAI's built-in metrics service |
| Native product analytics | Product usage, lifecycle and feature measurements | OpenAI's internal analytics transport; not a supported substitute for the customer OTel API |
| Workspace compliance records | Auditable product activity and content snapshots | Enterprise Compliance Logs Platform |
| Workspace analytics | Materialized usage, tokens, attribution and costs | Admin Analytics APIs |
| Inbound model/service metadata | Usage, rate limits and transport timing returned to a client | Response streams and headers; these are not automatically outgoing OTel records |

**Evidence labels matter.** A source-defined event has an emitter in the versioned implementation. A declared desktop analytics type has a literal declaration in the shipped bundle, but may be a nested payload type, a gated feature, or unused compatibility code. A documented cloud record has a public export contract. None of those, by itself, proves that an individual event was emitted by your account or reached a collector.

The catalogs deliberately retain experimental and compatibility entries. A name is not labeled deprecated merely because it is absent from one document, disabled locally, or unfamiliar. Dynamic names, runtime extensions, and proprietary server-only instrumentation cannot be exhaustively recovered from public documentation or a desktop binary. Those boundaries are stated rather than filled with invented names.


## Verified version boundaries

| Component | Observed version/evidence | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Terminal CLI | `codex --version` → `codex-cli 0.163.0` | Exact requested CLI version |
| ChatGPT macOS bundle | `CFBundleShortVersionString=26.1013.40934`; bundle build `20770`; identifier `com.openai.codex` | Exact requested desktop build |
| CLI embedded in that desktop bundle | `codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2` | Desktop and terminal version strings differ |
| Runtime source | OpenAI tags `rust-v0.163.0` and `rust-v0.163.0-alpha.10.2` | Shared Rust files in the downloaded trees were compared; no differing shared `.rs` files were found |
| Public Admin API | Downloaded OpenAPI information version `2.5.39` | Current server export schema, independently versioned from desktop and CLI |
| chatgpt.com / cloud services | Continuously deployed services | A desktop build number does not pin their backend implementation |

The installed versions above are verified. “Newest” is time- and rollout-dependent; this document pins the requested builds, rather than treating a version string as proof of every account's update channel.

Sources: [CLI 0.163.0 source](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/rust-v0.163.0), [desktop runtime source](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/rust-v0.163.0-alpha.10.2), [public Admin API reference](https://chatgpt.com/public/admin/api-reference), and the installed bundle metadata.


## The important answers before the catalogs

1. **The four surfaces do not have one interchangeable telemetry schema.** `codex.tool_result`, a desktop structured analytics message, a `CODEX_LOG` record and a daily usage row describe different layers.
2. **OTel logging is richer than the default trace-event path.** Detailed logs can include account email, tool arguments and output. The trace-safe event path omits selected sensitive fields, but is not a guarantee that every span or arbitrary custom attribute is content-free.
3. **`otel.log_user_prompt = false` is not a universal content-redaction switch.** It redacts the prompt field on the prompt event. Tool arguments/output, explicitly enabled final-answer logs, assessment rationale, feedback and compliance content have separate behavior.
4. **Version 0.163.0 contradicts part of the current public configuration prose:** `analytics.enabled = false` disables the built-in Statsig metrics route, but does **not** disable an explicitly configured custom OTLP metrics exporter. Disable that route with `otel.metrics_exporter = "none"`. The versioned implementation is authoritative for this manual.
5. **New cloud orchestration does not stream into the old local collector.** Supported local execution records can still arrive locally. Supported cloud records come from Compliance APIs. Repointing the local collector does not restore the missing cloud orchestration stream.
6. **The supplied singular cloud URL is the legacy guide.** New reusable cloud setups use the plural `cloud-environments` guide. Legacy workflows still include Code Review and GitHub/Linear integrations; the docs state an intention to deprecate that experience, not that every legacy workflow is already gone.

Sources: [0.163.0 exporter selection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/core/src/otel_init.rs), [log/trace filters](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/provider.rs), [cloud/local coverage](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/cloud-local-access#review-opentelemetry-and-audit-coverage), [new cloud](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments), [legacy cloud](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environment).


## What telemetry does on your Mac

Telemetry observes operations; it is not itself a grant of permission to edit files, control apps, record the screen, or operate a browser. Those capabilities belong to the underlying tools and their permissions. Telemetry can record that an operation was requested, decided, started, completed, failed, or timed out. Those states are not interchangeable.

Runtime instrumentation allocates counters and buffers, records timestamps and attributes, serializes batches and makes outbound collector requests when configured. Local diagnostic logging can write to Codex's bounded stores; an explicitly configured `log_dir` also enables the plaintext TUI log. A larger tool-output logging limit increases potential payload size and disclosure. Export failure is not proof that the underlying operation failed, and successful operation is not proof that export succeeded.

Native desktop product analytics is separate. The shipped app includes structured event transport, Statsig experiment/exposure handling, error reporting and native diagnostic logging. Static inclusion is not proof that every route is active in your account. This manual contains identifiers and schemas, not your private event values, credentials, conversation contents or captured network traffic.

Cloud-only work records activity on the cloud side. When a cloud task uses a local executor, that executor can generate local records too. A cloud `EXECUTION_REQUESTED` event means a launch was requested; an executor `process_exit` record supplies a different observation about the process outcome.

No telemetry settings were changed to prepare this document. The inspection used version output, installed static assets, versioned source and public schemas; it did not run test model tasks or turn on content export.


## Runtime configuration: exact OpenAI controls

The table describes the 0.163.0 runtime configuration model. Put telemetry routing in the user-level configuration or an applicable managed layer. Project-local telemetry routing is restricted. Exporter configuration and the consuming process's effective configuration must agree; a file edit alone does not prove a running daemon reloaded it.

| Key | Default / values | What it changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `analytics.enabled` | Optional Boolean; client default when unset | Consent for built-in analytics. In this version, custom OTLP metrics remain independently configured. |
| `otel.environment` | `"dev"` | Value of the native resource attribute `env`. |
| `otel.exporter` | `"none"`; OTLP HTTP or gRPC configuration | Detailed log export destination. |
| `otel.trace_exporter` | `"none"`; OTLP HTTP or gRPC configuration | Span export destination. Enabling logs does not implicitly enable traces. |
| `otel.metrics_exporter` | `"statsig"`; `"none"`; OTLP HTTP or gRPC configuration | Metrics destination. The built-in Statsig path applies an explicit metric exclusion list. |
| `otel.log_user_prompt` | `false` | Whether `codex.user_prompt` includes raw prompt text in detailed logs. |
| `otel.log_agent_responses` | `false` | Opt-in final main-agent/spawned-subagent answer logs; requires an explicit OTLP log destination. |
| `otel.log_guardian_assessments` | `false` | Opt-in completed automatic-review assessment logs; requires an explicit OTLP log destination. |
| `otel.tool_result.max_bytes` | `2048` | UTF-8 byte limit on tool-output previews, before an added truncation notice. Does not limit model-visible output or tool arguments. |
| `otel.span_attributes` | Empty string-to-string map | Additional attributes attached to exported spans; arbitrary keys make the possible attribute set open-ended. |
| `otel.tracestate` | Empty nested map | Adds/updates W3C tracestate member fields; validated independently from span attributes. |
| `otel.<exporter>.otlp-http.endpoint` | Explicit endpoint | Signal-specific HTTP destination. Use the proper logs, traces or metrics path for that collector. |
| `otel.<exporter>.otlp-http.protocol` | `binary` or `json` | OTLP HTTP serialization. |
| `otel.<exporter>.otlp-http.headers` | Map | Request headers; values can be credentials and should not be copied into diagnostics. |
| `otel.<exporter>.otlp-grpc.endpoint` | Explicit endpoint | gRPC collector destination. |
| `otel.<exporter>.otlp-grpc.headers` | Map | gRPC exporter metadata/header configuration. |
| `otel.<exporter>.<transport>.tls.ca-certificate` | Optional path | Trust root for the collector. |
| `otel.<exporter>.<transport>.tls.client-certificate` | Optional path | Client TLS certificate. |
| `otel.<exporter>.<transport>.tls.client-private-key` | Optional path | Client TLS key. |
| `features.runtime_metrics` | Under development; false in the inspected CLI | Enables the runtime metrics reader/summary facilities; not the general export switch. |
| `features.analytics_plan_history` | Experimental; true in the inspected CLI | Plan allowance history preview in `/analytics`; not a raw telemetry exporter. |
| `feedback.enabled` | Normally `true` | Whether supported local clients accept feedback submissions. |
| `log_dir` | Runtime log location; explicit setting enables plaintext TUI log | Local diagnostic files, independent from an OTLP collector. |
| `RUST_LOG` | Client-dependent filter | Local diagnostic verbosity. Debug/trace verbosity can expose more implementation detail. |
| `history.persistence` | `save-all` or `none` | Input history policy; do not interpret this as a universal deletion switch for all thread, diagnostic, cloud or analytics storage. |
| `history.max_bytes` | Optional byte limit | Bound for the input-history file. |

Here `<exporter>` means `exporter`, `trace_exporter` or `metrics_exporter`; `<transport>` means `otlp-http` or `otlp-grpc`. The configuration types share exporter structures, but Statsig is intended for metrics. These are configuration keys, not emitted attributes.

An explicit all-three-runtime-exporters-off fragment is:

```toml
[analytics]
enabled = false

[otel]
exporter = "none"
trace_exporter = "none"
metrics_exporter = "none"
log_user_prompt = false
log_agent_responses = false
log_guardian_assessments = false
```

This fragment is illustrative, not applied. It is not a promise to turn off every hosted audit record, service operational log, desktop crash route or browser-site analytic. Those have distinct owners and policies.

Sources: [configuration types](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/config/src/types.rs), [configuration defaults](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/core/src/config/otel.rs), [exporter selection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/core/src/otel_init.rs), [tool preview limit](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/protocol/src/config_types.rs), [local diagnostics](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/environment-variables).


## Resource attributes, shared event fields and units

| Name | Placement | Meaning / qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `service.name` | Resource | Host-selected service/originator identity; do not hard-code one value for every client. |
| `service.version` | Resource | Emitting runtime version. |
| `env` | Resource | OpenAI's native environment label. It is not automatically renamed to an upstream deployment attribute. |
| `host.name` | Detailed-log resource when available | Local machine hostname. Intentionally omitted from the corresponding trace resource builder. |
| `os`, `os_version` | Metric resource when resolved | Sanitized OS type/version. These are the native keys in this runtime. |
| `event.name` | Named event | Exact event discriminator. |
| `event.timestamp` | Shared event field | UTC RFC3339 time with milliseconds, where the emitter adds it. |
| `conversation.id` | Shared event field | Runtime thread/conversation correlation identifier. |
| `app.version` | Shared field / metric tag | Runtime version; distinct from desktop bundle version and resource placement. |
| `auth_mode` | Shared field / metric tag | Authentication mode reported by the emitting client. |
| `originator` | Shared field / metric tag | Client origin. Metrics constrain known originators; unknown values map to `other`. |
| `terminal.type` | Shared event field | Terminal identification. |
| `model`, `slug` | Shared event fields | Configured/selected model identifiers recorded by the runtime. |
| `user.account_id`, `user.email` | Detailed-log shared fields | Account identity; omitted by the trace-safe shared event macro. |
| `user.id` | Selected detailed events | User identifier, for example skill invocation. Not universally present. |
| `session_source` | Metric tag | CLI, executor, editor or other session provenance, when added by the session metrics wrapper. |
| `service_name` | Optional metric tag | Metric service attribution; distinct spelling and placement from resource `service.name`. |
| `product_sku` | Selected signals | Bounded product attribution; this source accepts `codex` and normalizes other nonempty values to `other`. |

The common-field list applies to emitters using the shared macros. It is not a universal required-field schema for every named diagnostic or executor event. Optional values can be absent. Global/process metrics do not all pass through the same session wrapper.

Durations ending `_ms` are milliseconds; executor metrics ending `_seconds` use seconds. `codex.goal.duration_s` uses seconds. `codex.turn.cost_microusd` accumulates millionths of USD. Some detailed event durations are formatted as strings by the tracing emitter. Preserve actual wire types rather than assuming every duration is a numeric attribute. A histogram of tool-call counts is not a counter, even when its name contains `call`.

Sources: [shared event macros](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/events/shared.rs), [metric tags](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/metrics/tags.rs), [metric resource construction](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/metrics/client.rs).


## Content handling and correlation details

`codex.tool_result` detailed logs contain raw arguments and a bounded output preview. `output_truncated` says that the telemetry preview was shortened; it does not certify that the original tool output was complete. `tool_result_seq` orders result recording across the process, not tool starts, and resets when the process restarts. The trace-safe counterpart records lengths, line count and origin instead of arguments/output content.

`codex.agent_response` is separately opted in, logs only eligible live final-answer items, deduplicates within a turn, and caps exported text at 65,536 UTF-8 bytes. It skips internal/review/compaction/memory-consolidation sessions. Exported memory citations are stripped from the copy; stored conversation history is not rewritten.

`codex.guardian_assessment` is separately opted in. It records terminal review status and, when available, outcome, risk and authorization classification. Failure/timeout/cancellation need not have a model outcome. The rationale cap is 65,536 bytes. A fail-closed denial is not evidence that a model classified the action as denied.

`codex.skill_invocation` records detected use and scope, not successful task completion. It omits skill contents and resource paths. Authentication storage metrics use bounded classifications rather than passwords or tokens. Authentication diagnostics can indicate that an environment variable/header is present without including its secret value.

On `codex.sse_event`, the historical field `tool_token_count` is assigned from `usage.total_tokens`. It therefore means total token usage in this emitter, despite the misleading name; it must not be added again as a separate tool-token category.

The new cloud/local join is explicit: cloud `CODEX_LOG / EXECUTION_REQUESTED` contains `launch_trace_id` and `launch_span_id`; local executor lifecycle logs retain them as `launch.trace_id` and `launch.span_id`. Keep the associated workspace/thread/tool identifiers too. Do not join unrelated products merely because they have fields named `session_id` or `conversation.id`.

Sources: [tool-result emitter](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/tool_result.rs), [answer emitter](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/agent_response.rs), [assessment emitter](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/guardian_assessment.rs), [executor lifecycle](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/exec-server/src/process_telemetry.rs), [Codex compliance contract](https://chatgpt.com/public/admin/api-reference).

### How the runtime carries trace context

The runtime can read `TRACEPARENT` and optional `TRACESTATE` from its environment. The environment-derived context is initialized once per process. Invalid incoming context is ignored; it does not fall back to an unrelated active span. For supported outgoing HTTP paths, the supplied span’s valid context replaces existing `traceparent`/`tracestate` headers. Configured `otel.tracestate` entries are merged into that context. These mechanisms carry correlation; they do not grant authorization or prove that the receiving service exported a span. [Implementation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/otel/src/trace_context.rs).


## Inbound OpenAI usage, rate-limit and timing metadata

These are service-to-client records. They should not be counted as additional outbound OTel event families.

| Name | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `codex.rate_limits` | Parsed stream event with plan_type, rate_limits.primary/secondary, credits, metered_limit_name and legacy limit_name. Windows contain used_percent, optional window_minutes and reset_at. Credits contain has_credits, unlimited and optional balance. |
| `x-{limit}-primary-used-percent`, `x-{limit}-primary-window-minutes`, `x-{limit}-primary-reset-at` | Primary allowance-window response headers; the default family uses codex and additional metered families are discovered. |
| `x-{limit}-secondary-used-percent`, `x-{limit}-secondary-window-minutes`, `x-{limit}-secondary-reset-at` | Secondary allowance-window response headers. |
| `x-{limit}-limit-name` | Human-facing meter/limit name when supplied. |
| `codex.response.metadata` | Recognized in the stream dispatch but ignored by the pinned handler branch; do not invent a customer export schema. |
| `responsesapi.websocket_timing` | Supplies timing_metrics values used for API overhead, inference, TTFT and time-between-token histograms. |
| `response.completed` | Supplies usage that can populate completion events and per-turn aggregation; not every stream frame has token counts. |

[Rate-limit parser](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/codex-api/src/rate_limits.rs), [stream handler](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs).


## Native product analytics in the CLI/runtime

This is a separate serialized-event client, with a destination formed as `<base_url>/codex/analytics-events/events`. It is not the configured OTel log endpoint. Eligibility and authentication are handled by the analytics client; some plugin-related records have explicit API-key support. The debug-only `CODEX_ANALYTICS_EVENTS_CAPTURE_FILE` can redirect these payloads to a local capture file in debug builds; it is not a supported release-build switch for capturing everything.

### Analytics payload structures

The following structures are reachable through the serialized `TrackEventsRequest` envelope. In-process queue, reducer and bookkeeping structs are excluded because they are not payload schemas. These are implementation schemas, not a promise of a public ingestion API. `Option<T>` is optional at the source level; exact omission/null behavior also depends on serialization annotations. `Vec<T>` is a list. Flattened fields should be expanded by the serializer, not treated as a mandatory nested object.

#### CodexAcceptedLineFingerprintsEventParams

Codex Accepted Line Fingerprints Event Params. [source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.163.0/codex-rs/analytics/src/events.rs#L179)

| Field | Source type | Meaning / serialization |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event_type` | `&'static str` | Native serialized event discriminator; interpretation depends on its envelope. |
| `turn_id` | `String` | Turn identifier. |
| `thread_id` | `String` | Thread identifier. |
| `product_surface` | `Option<String>` | Product surface selected for this activity’s attribution. |
| `model_slug` | `Option<String>` | Selected model’s catalog identifier. |
| `completed_at` | `u64` | Completion timestamp in the unit defined by this source payload. |
| `repo_hash` | `Option<String>` | Hash of the normalized repository remote used for attribution; not the raw remote URL. |
| `accepted_added_lines` | `u64` | Number of accepted added lines attributed to the tool’s changes. |
| `accepted_deleted_lines` | `u64` | Number of accepted deleted lines attributed to the tool’s changes. |
| `line_fingerprints` | `[(); 0]` | Analytics ingestion and warehouse schemas require this field on the wire. Keep it statically empty; line fingerprints are no longer generated. |

## ChatGPT desktop 26.1013.40934: additional client analytics

The installed Electron bundle contains a separate structured analytics implementation. It can form a Statsig or Segment-style envelope, with an event ID, event creation time, event type, event parameters and an `@type` marker. The marker is formed from `openai.buf.dev/openai/protobuf-analytics-events/` plus the declared protobuf analytics type. Client metadata, device/user/account context and transport choice depend on the path. These are internal schemas, not a supported user-selectable OTel collector interface.

The bundle also includes Statsig exposure identifiers (`statsig::gate_exposure`, `statsig::config_exposure`, `statsig::layer_exposure`), diagnostic/error integrations and native telemetry-user updates. A library or identifier being bundled does not prove the feature is enabled or that data was transmitted. No claims about your actual historical activity are made here.

### Desktop structured-event envelope

The installed bundle has two builders. Both place event-specific fields inside `eventParams`; the Segment-style builder explicitly adds more identity/context fields. The Statsig builder’s smaller local envelope does not establish that the SDK adds no identity metadata later.

| Field/path | Builder | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eventId` | Both | Generated event identifier |
| `eventCreatedAt` | Both | Supplied creation time or the current ISO timestamp |
| `eventType` | Both | Literal `web` in these builders, even though they are bundled in the desktop app |
| `deviceParams` | Both | Empty object at this construction step |
| `eventParams.@type` | Both | Protobuf analytics type URL identifying the payload |
| `eventParams.<event-specific fields>` | Both | Fields supplied by the event’s caller; not a uniform global schema |
| `punchOutInfoToken` | Both | Opaque value returned by the instrumentation context; its consumer schema is not exposed here |
| `clientMetadata.name` | Segment-style | App name supplied to the analytics client |
| `clientMetadata.version` | Segment-style | App version supplied to the analytics client |
| `userParams.userId` | Segment-style | User ID, or an empty string for the unsigned-in path |
| `userParams.deviceId` | Segment-style | Analytics client device ID |
| `userParams.authStatus` | Segment-style | Logged-in/logged-out classification |
| `userParams.adsSegmentId` | Segment-style, conditional | Ads segment value when supplied as an integer within signed 32-bit range |
| `userParams.planType` | Segment-style, conditional | Plan trait |
| `userParams.workspaceId` | Segment-style, conditional | Workspace trait |
| `userParams.organizationId` | Segment-style, conditional | Organization ID taken from available custom IDs |
| `userParams.isOpenaiInternal` | Segment-style, conditional | Internal-account trait |
| `statsigMetadataV2.stableId` | Segment-style, conditional | Stable ID from the Statsig context; distinct from a conversation ID |
| `statsigMetadataV2.sdkType`, `.sdkVersion` | Segment-style, conditional | SDK identification |
| `statsigMetadataV2.sessionId` | Segment-style, conditional | Statsig session ID; do not equate it with a Codex thread ID |
| `statsigMetadataV2.appIdentifier`, `.appVersion` | Segment-style, conditional | App identity/version copied into this metadata block |
| `statsigMetadataV2.locale`, `.language` | Segment-style, conditional | Locale and its leading language component |
| `statsigMetadataV2.user.userId` | Segment-style, conditional | Statsig user ID |
| `statsigMetadataV2.user.customIds` | Segment-style, conditional | String-valued custom IDs |
| `statsigMetadataV2.user.email`, `.ip`, `.userAgent` | Segment-style, conditional | Available email, IP and user-agent context; sensitive identifying fields |
| `statsigMetadataV2.user.country`, `.locale`, `.appVersion` | Segment-style, conditional | Available locale/country/version user context |
| `statsigMetadataV2.user.custom` | Segment-style, conditional | Custom metadata values serialized to JSON strings when serialization succeeds |
| `eventParams.sourceSurfaceStableId` | Selected event types, conditional | Added from a configured custom ID, or a qualifying ChatGPT client device ID; absent/oversized values are not used |

The normalized diagnostic event name uses the final type-name segment and converts CamelCase to snake_case. This normalization is not proof that every declared protobuf type is emitted. Expected user/account checks can stop delivery after context changes. The local `analytics_event_tracked` counter records an analytics code path; it is not a collector receipt or server-side retention guarantee.

Evidence: installed `app.asar` → `webview/assets/app-initial-90eb42395b7d.js`, `buildSegmentEnvelope` near character 3,314,848; `buildStatsigEnvelope` near 3,316,423; `sendStructuredEvent` near 3,318,204. These are static observations for desktop 26.1013.40934, not a capture of your event values and not a version pin for chatgpt.com.

### Desktop payload fields found at call sites

This expands the declaration catalog with statically visible payloads. The analysis resolved local bindings and named imports/exports across 347 bundle modules. It found 1722 calls referencing 1015 declared type descriptors, with 4014 distinct type/field pairs. A reference is evidence that code passes that descriptor and payload to a function; it is not proof that the function ran or that a service accepted the event.

Field paths are the union of visible object properties at those references, including resolvable object initializers and inline payload callbacks. Dots below express nested object paths. They are not invented dotted JSON keys. These are not required-field schemas. Object spreads, computed keys, helper calls, function arguments, mutations and account-dependent branches can add, remove or transform fields. Dynamic payloads are marked; absence from a static payload is not proof that a runtime field never exists.

The value column preserves literal values and uppercase enum members visible in expressions. It is a subset observed in code, not the complete allowed-value domain. A runtime expression means the value is supplied or computed; it does not mean the value is always present. S-number references are local to each type. Their offsets use JavaScript UTF-16 indexing in the extracted bundle file, whereas declaration offsets above use Unicode character indexing. No private runtime values were captured.

Common correlation fields such as `conversationId`, `threadId`, `turnId`, `messageId`, `sessionId`, `workspaceId`, `organizationId`, `userId` and `requestId` retain the identity domain stated by their names. `action`, `surface`, `source`, `stage`, `result`, `outcome`, `reason` and `status` are event-specific classifications; their domains must not be merged merely because the keys match. Fields ending in `Ms` name milliseconds; other timing units must be checked at their source. Counts, flags, content fields and identifiers are not interchangeable.

## chatgpt.com and new Codex Cloud: public export contracts

These services expose workspace records and aggregated analytics. They do not promise that every local `codex.*` event has a corresponding cloud record. The desktop’s embedded web assets are also not proof of the exact JavaScript or server experiment active on chatgpt.com at another time.

The new cloud environment guide is [Cloud environments](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments). The supplied [singular cloud-environment URL](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environment) documents **Codex Cloud (Legacy)**. Creating a new cloud environment, publishing a snapshot, and continuing an existing task have different lifecycle effects; do not assume one environment event covers every snapshot/task transition.

For cloud orchestration with local computer access, collect supported local execution OTel and supported cloud Compliance records separately. The new cloud record `EXECUTION_REQUESTED` supplies the launch trace/span pair for joining to executor events. This is best-effort correlation; it does not establish successful execution. [Cloud/local audit coverage](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/cloud-local-access#review-opentelemetry-and-audit-coverage).

### Public log families

The family selector on a file-list request is named `event_type`. Inside a JSONL record, the outer `type` identifies its family; families such as `CODEX_LOG` also contain an inner `event_type` for the action. These levels must not be flattened into one ambiguous field.

| Record `type` | What it records | Main payload shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONVERSATION_MESSAGE` | Message snapshot | `previous_message_id`, `message`, `conversation` |
| `APP_LOG` | App invocation request or response | `app_id`, `app_name`, `app_type`, `conversation_id`, `log_type`, `input`, `output` |
| `APP_AUTH_LOG` | App linkage change | `app_id`, `link_id`, `action` (`link` / `unlink`) |
| `AUDIT_LOG` | Workspace/user/admin action | `action`, `action_result`, `action_privilege`, `request_metadata`, `action_data` |
| `AUTH_LOG` | Authentication action | `request_metadata`, `action_data` |
| `CODEX_LOG` | Codex product action | `event_type`, `client_id`, `agent`, `workspace_id`, `event_details` |
| `CODEX_TURN` | Materialized turn analytics | `payload` with turn, model, usage, skill/plugin and artifact attribution |
| `CHATGPT_PLUGIN_SPREADSHEET` | Spreadsheet plugin prompt/response | `event_type`, `client_id`, `workspace_id`, `event_details` |
| `CHATGPT_PLUGIN_PRESENTATION` | Presentation plugin prompt/response | Same family-specific envelope pattern |
| `CHATGPT_PLUGIN_DOCUMENT` | Document plugin prompt/response | Presentation-style schema with Word client identity |
| `CODEX_SECURITY_LOG` | Security scan/remediation activity | `event_type`, `client_id`, `workspace_id`, `event_details` |
| `CUSTOM_AGENTS_LOG` | Workspace Agent lifecycle/run/tool activity | `event_type`, `client_id`, `workspace_id`, `event_details` |
| `COSTS` | Hourly paid-plan usage and billing measures | Organization-scoped `payload` |

Source for the cloud record/schema tables in this chapter: [OpenAI public Admin API reference, OpenAPI 2.5.39](https://chatgpt.com/public/admin/api-reference).

### Shared compliance envelope

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event_id` | Stable deduplication identifier |
| `type` | Log family |
| `timestamp` | Event/action time in UTC; not necessarily ingestion time |
| `principal.id` | Owning workspace/organization ID |
| `principal.type` | `CHATGPT_WORKSPACE` or `API_PLATFORM_ORG` |
| `actor.type` | Actor variant; affects the available identity fields |
| `actor.user_id`, `actor.user_email` | Account-user identity, where applicable |
| `actor.credential_id` | Non-secret PAT identifier when applicable |
| `actor.redacted_id` | Redacted API-key identity for API-key actors |
| `actor.provider`, `actor.provider_tenant_id`, `actor.provider_user_id` | External collaboration actor identity |
| `actor.id` | System actor identifier where the family uses a system actor |

The file API is at-least-once: deduplicate by `event_id`. Files are immutable; event updates can therefore produce additional records. Freshness reports the maximum retained event time, not a guarantee that every earlier event has arrived. The general file retention window is 30 days; specialized materialized data has different latency. `CODEX_TURN` is generated approximately two hours after its source hour; `COSTS` expects roughly three to five hours.

### CODEX_LOG: every documented sub-event

Every `event_details` variant has `detail_type`. Optional fields and availability vary with the emitting client.

| `event_type` | Meaning | Additional `event_details` keys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ENVIRONMENT_CREATED` | Environment created | `environment_id`, `environment_fields` |
| `ENVIRONMENT_UPDATED` | Environment changed | `environment_id`, `environment_fields` |
| `ENVIRONMENT_DELETED` | Environment deleted | `environment_id` |
| `WORKSPACE_UPDATED` | Workspace settings changed | `previous_settings`, `current_settings` |
| `PROMPT_SENT` | Prompt submitted | `session_id`, `prompt_text`, `turn_id`, `call_id`, `model`, `environment_id` |
| `PROMPT_RESPONSE_RECEIVED` | Response received | `session_id`, `response_text`, `status`, `turn_id`, `call_id`, `model`, `service_tier`, `reasoning_effort`, `token_usage`, `environment_id` |
| `TOOL_CALL_SUGGESTED` | Tool call proposed | `session_id`, `tool_name`, `tool_type`, `tool_input`, `turn_id`, `call_id`, `tool_call_id`, `status`, `model`, `environment_id` |
| `TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED` | Tool call completed | Same tool-call key family |
| `TOOL_CALL_FAILED` | Tool call failed | Same tool-call key family |
| `TOOL_DECISION` | Cloud tool approval decision | `session_id`, `tool_call_id`, `tool_name`, `decision`, `source` |
| `EXECUTION_REQUESTED` | Cloud requested executor launch | `session_id`, `tool_call_id`, `tool_name`, `launch_trace_id`, `launch_span_id` |
| `ACCESS_TOKEN_CREATED` | Token created | `access_token_id`, `access_token_name`, `created_by_user_id`, `expires_at` |
| `ACCESS_TOKEN_REVOKED` | Token revoked | Same token key family |
| `APP_MCP_CALL` | App MCP invocation | `call_id`, `name`, `arguments`, `tool_meta` |
| `APP_MCP_RESULT` | App MCP result | `call_id`, `name`, `status`, `error_code`, `error_message`, `result_preview` |
| `APP_MCP_ELICITATION` | App MCP question/approval lifecycle | `call_id`, `name`, `elicitation_type`, `phase`, `decision`, `url` |
| `PLUGIN_CREATED` | Plugin created | Plugin key family below |
| `PLUGIN_EDITED` | Plugin edited/published | Plugin key family below |
| `PLUGIN_DELETED` | Plugin deleted | Plugin key family below |
| `PLUGIN_INSTALLED` | Plugin installed | Plugin key family below |
| `PLUGIN_UNINSTALLED` | Plugin uninstalled | Plugin key family below |
| `SITE_PROJECT_CREATED` | Site project created | `project_id`, `slug` |
| `SITE_PROJECT_DELETED` | Site project deleted | `project_id`, `slug` |
| `SITE_VERSION_CREATED` | Site version created | `project_id`, `version_id`, `version_number` |
| `SITE_DEPLOYMENT_STARTED` | Site deployment started | `project_id`, `version_id`, `deployment_id`, `environment_revision` |
| `SITE_DEPLOYMENT_COMPLETED` | Site deployment terminal result | `project_id`, `version_id`, `deployment_id`, `status`, `environment_revision`, `site_url` |

Plugin key family: `plugin_id`, `plugin_release_id`, `plugin_version`, `plugin_name`, `plugin_display_name`, `marketplace_name`, `plugin_scope`, `plugin_creator_account_user_id`. Scope values are `GLOBAL`, `WORKSPACE`, `USER`. Response `token_usage` contains `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, `reasoning_output_tokens`.

Cloud decision values: `approved`, `approved_with_amendment`, `approved_for_session`, `approved_mcp_policy_amendment`, `approved_with_network_policy_allow`, `denied_with_network_policy_deny`, `denied`, `timed_out`, `abort`. Decision source can be `automated_reviewer`, `config`, or `user`. These decisions do not contain prompt, tool-argument or output content. Tool-call IDs differ from inference request IDs.

`agent` contains `type`, optional verified deployment `id`, and optional `name`; legacy `agent_id` and `agent_name` remain compatibility fields. Do not merge agent identity and human actor identity.

### CONVERSATION_MESSAGE: field inventory

| Field/path | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `previous_message_id` | Previous message for reconstruction |
| `message.id`, `message.created_at` | Message identity and creation time |
| `message.author.type` | `user` / `assistant` author discriminator |
| `message.author.client_type` | User-message client surface |
| `message.author.model` | Assistant model |
| `message.author.tools_used`, `skills_used`, `skills_used_names` | Tool/skill attribution |
| `message.author.applied_custom_instructions` | Applied raw custom instructions when available |
| `message.content.type` | `text`, `user_instructions`, or `quotation` |
| `message.content.value` | Text/instruction content |
| `message.content.annotations[].type` | `url_citation`, `file_citation`, or `custom_action` |
| `message.content.annotations[].urls` | Cited URLs |
| `message.content.annotations[].files[].id`, `.name` | Cited file identity/name |
| `message.content.annotations[].action_domain`, `.action_name` | Custom action attribution |
| `message.content.file_id`, `.file_name`, `.quote` | Quotation source and text |
| `message.files[].id`, `.name` | Attached file identity/name |
| `conversation.id`, `.title` | Conversation identity/title |
| `conversation.mode` | `chat` / `work`, when supplied |
| `conversation.gpt_id`, `.gpt_name` | GPT identity/name |
| `conversation.project_id`, `.project_name` | Project identity/name |
| `conversation.created_at` | Conversation creation time |
| `conversation.is_pinned`, `.is_temporary_chat` | Snapshot flags |
| `conversation.is_locked_chat` | Snapshot flag; missing historical value means unknown, not false |

User client types: `unknown`, `desktop_web`, `ios_web`, `ios_app`, `macos_app`, `windows_app`, `android_web`, `android_app`, `chatgpt_api`. Group by conversation, order using message relationships, and retain updates sharing a message ID rather than confusing message identity with event identity.

### CODEX_TURN: materialized turn payload

Fields under `payload`: `hour_partition`, `turn_id`, `turn_key`, `thread_id`, `session_id`, `product_client_id`, `model`, `reasoning_effort`, `speed`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `duration_ms`, `response_count`, `classification`, `credits`, `cost_usd`, `estimated_cost_usd`, `tags`, `token_usage`, `skills`, `plugins`, `artifact_actions`.

| Nested structure | Keys / values |
| --- | --- |
| `classification` | `taxonomy_version`, `level_1`, `level_2` |
| `token_usage` | `uncached_input_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, `output_tokens` |
| `skills[]` | `skill_id`, `skill_name`, `skill_scope`, `call_count` |
| `plugins[]` | `plugin_id`, `plugin_name`, `plugin_category`, `marketplace_name`, `call_count` |
| `artifact_actions[]` | `artifact_kind`, `action`, `action_count` |
| `artifact_kind` | `spreadsheet`, `document`, `presentation`, `pdf` in V1 |
| `action` | `produced`, `edited` in V1 |
| `tags[]` | Contains `automation` for an automation-initiated turn; otherwise empty |

This is an hourly materialized view, not the raw local turn stream. Later enrichment does not rewrite already emitted files. `cost_usd` is native USD usage; `estimated_cost_usd` estimates the credit portion. They are not interchangeable and neither is a final invoice.

### COSTS: organization-scoped hourly data

`COSTS` uses the **organization** logs route and `API_PLATFORM_ORG`; it is not available from the workspace logs route. Its payload keys are `day`, `hour`, `organization_id`, `identity`, `product`, `surface`, `client`, `model`, `service_tier`, `reasoning`, `measures`.

`identity` can contain `user_id`, `email`, `name`, `groups[]` (`id`, `name`) and `agent` (`id`, `name`). `measures.usage` can contain `text_input_tokens`, `text_cached_input_tokens`, `text_output_tokens`, `audio_input_tokens`, `audio_cached_input_tokens`, `audio_output_tokens`, `image_input_tokens`, `image_cached_input_tokens`, `image_output_tokens`, or aggregate `text_total_tokens`, `audio_total_tokens`, `image_total_tokens`.

Each `measures.billing[]` entry has `sku`, `quantity` (`value`, `unit`), `cost` (`value`, `unit`), and optional `estimated_cost_usd` (`value`, `unit`). Preserve `CREDITS` versus `USD`. The estimate applies to credit-priced entries; native USD should not be converted again. Negative adjustments and zero values retain their original unit.

### App, authentication, security and agent records

`APP_LOG.app_type` values: `SERVICE`, `OPEN_API`, `MCP`, `FIRST_PARTY_ECOSYSTEM`, `UNKNOWN`. Request and response are separate observations; a response may never arrive. App-specific extra fields are not a stable universal schema. `APP_AUTH_LOG.app_id` can be null after unlink/removal.

`AUDIT_LOG.action_result`: `SUCCESS`, `BLOCKED`, `ERROR`. `action_privilege`: `ADMIN`, `STANDARD_USER`. Request metadata can include `client_ip`, `client_ip_details`, `client_user_agent`, `client_ja3`, `client_ja4`, `destination_hostname`. The full action-name catalog follows later.

Channel audit actions additionally include `AGENT_RUN_COMPLETED`, `AGENT_TASK_DELEGATED`, `CODE_ENVIRONMENT_ACCESSED`. Their shared correlation fields are `flow_id`, reserved `flow_binding`, and optional verified `requester_account_user_id`. Slack attribution uses `slack_team_id`, `slack_user_id`, `slack_channel_id`, `slack_event_id`; Teams attribution uses `microsoft_teams_tenant_id`, `microsoft_teams_team_id`, `microsoft_teams_channel_id`, `microsoft_teams_user_aad_object_id`, `microsoft_teams_event_id`. Completion adds `execution_backend`, `failure_reason`; delegation adds `delegated_task_id`, `delegation_request_id`, `delegation_status`, `delegated_workflow_id`; environment access adds `environment_type`, `environment_name`, `environment_access_id`, `environment_status`.

`CODEX_SECURITY_LOG` sub-events: `SCAN_CONFIGURATION_CREATED`, `SCAN_CONFIGURATION_UPDATED`, `SCAN_FINDING_UPDATED`, `PROPOSED_PATCH_PR_CREATED`. They carry scan configuration/finding IDs, sanitized field snapshots or changes, and a PR URL when available. They are product audit observations, not proof that a vulnerability is fixed.

`CUSTOM_AGENTS_LOG` sub-events: `AGENT_CREATED`, `AGENT_DELETED`, `AGENT_PUBLISHED`, `AGENT_RUN_COMPLETED`, `AGENT_RUN_CREATED`, `AGENT_RUN_FAILED`, `AGENT_RUN_MESSAGE`, `AGENT_UPDATED`, `CONNECTOR_CALL_COMPLETED`, `CONNECTOR_CALL_REQUESTED`, `CONNECTOR_OAUTH_RESOLVED`, `MEMORY_DELETE`, `MEMORY_READ`, `MEMORY_WRITE`, `SKILL_USED`, `TRIGGER_CREATED`, `TRIGGER_DELETED`, `TRIGGER_UPDATED`. Agent/version/run/tool-call IDs provide lifecycle correlation. Connector, memory, skill and trigger payloads differ by action. The field-token appendix below preserves the additional documented keys.

Spreadsheet, presentation and document plugin sub-events are `PROMPT_SENT` and `PROMPT_RESPONSE_RECEIVED`. Spreadsheet client IDs include `BASISPOINTS_EXCEL_ADDIN`, `BASISPOINTS_SHEETS_ADDIN`, `BASISPOINTS_SIMULATOR`, `BASISPOINTS_UNKNOWN_DEFAULT`. Presentation uses `BASISPOINTS_POWERPOINT_ADDIN`; document uses `BASISPOINTS_WORD_ADDIN`. The details contain session, prompt/response, model and usage fields as appropriate.

### Analytics API routes and semantics

The native base is `https://api.chatgpt.com/v1`; routes below omit that prefix.

| GET route | Meaning | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/analytics/workspaces/{workspace_id}/usage` | Unified daily ChatGPT, Codex and Work usage | Current |
| `/analytics/codex/workspaces/{workspace_id}/turn-insights` | Turn/cost rollups and classification grouping | Current |
| `/analytics/codex/workspaces/{workspace_id}/usage` | Older Codex-only daily usage | Deprecated; planned retirement 2026-12-15 |
| `/analytics/codex/workspaces/{workspace_id}/code_reviews` | Daily review/comment/severity counts | Current; not covered by the usage deprecation |
| `/analytics/codex/workspaces/{workspace_id}/code_review_responses` | Replies/reactions to review comments | Current; not covered by the usage deprecation |

Daily usage parameters: `workspace_id`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `limit`, `group`, `page`; `group=workspace` selects a workspace aggregate. Turn-insights parameters: `workspace_id`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `agent_types`, `group_ids`, `user_ids`, `group_by[]`, `page`. Grouping values: `agent_type`, `classification.level_1`, `classification.level_2`; agent types: `codex`, `work`.

Unified `chats` includes ChatGPT chats and Codex threads; `messages` includes ChatGPT messages and Codex turns. Those are operational measures, not a count of humans actively engaged. Deleted-user inclusion differs between per-user and workspace aggregation. Preserve UTC date/window semantics and pagination. Missing token or cost coverage must not be converted to zero.

The unified scope is `enterprise.analytics.usage.read`; the Codex-specific analytics scope is `codex.enterprise.analytics.read`. They are not interchangeable. A normal model API project key is not a workspace Admin key. [Analytics overview](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/analytics-api).


## OpenAI metadata visible to MCP/plugin servers

These are request-context metadata, not automatic OpenTelemetry attributes. A server can choose to instrument them according to its own policy and schema.

| Metadata key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `_meta["openai/locale"]` | Requested BCP-47 locale |
| `_meta["webplus/i18n"]` | Older locale key retained for client compatibility |
| `_meta["openai/userAgent"]` | Optional best-effort user-agent hint; not a stable host detector |
| `_meta["openai/userLocation"]` | Coarse location object; keys can include city, region, country, timezone, longitude, latitude |
| `_meta["openai/subject"]` | Anonymized user identifier |
| `_meta["openai/session"]` | Anonymized conversation identifier |
| `_meta["openai/organization"]` | Anonymized organization identifier when available |

Treat hints as optional and unsuitable for authorization. Do not assume the anonymized session identifier equals the local Codex thread UUID. Source: [OpenAI plugin metadata reference](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/reference).


## Experimental, deprecated, compatibility and unavailable surfaces

| Item | Exact interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| `features.analytics_plan_history` | Experimental allowance-history UI. Not a generic telemetry export. |
| `features.runtime_metrics` | Under-development runtime metrics reader. |
| Guardian V2 metric/event families | Development-gated paths in the pinned source; not evidence they ran in this account. |
| Skill shadow-selection metric family | Experimental selection/measurement path. |
| Desktop declared-only types | Maturity and live emission unknown unless separately documented; retained in the appendix rather than mislabeled stable. |
| `CODEX_ANALYTICS_EVENTS_CAPTURE_FILE` | Debug-build-only native analytics capture; release builds do not enable it. |
| `line_fingerprints` | Compatibility field kept empty in current native accepted-line analytics. |
| `agent_id`, `agent_name` on Codex compliance records | Legacy fields retained alongside structured `agent`. |
| `_meta["webplus/i18n"]` | Older locale metadata spelling. |
| `chatgpt.enterprise.compliance_export.read` | Legacy broad read scope still accepted; fine-grained/broad Logs Platform scopes are the current interface. |
| Old Codex daily usage endpoint | Deprecated with planned retirement on 15 December 2026. |
| Codex Cloud (Legacy) | Still documented for specific integrations; replacement cloud environment model is separate. |
| `item/fileChange/outputDelta` | Deprecated app-server compatibility notification, no longer emitted by current versions; use fileChange items and turn diff updates. It is a protocol notification, not an OTel event. |
| Public `codex.websocket_event` log example | The pinned session telemetry implementation records WebSocket event **metrics**; no corresponding named log emitter was found. Do not fabricate the log from the documentation’s representative list. |
| Older documentation-only metric names | Listed separately above; absence from this version is a discrepancy, not proof of a formal retirement policy. |
| Private cloud/backend metrics and experiment schemas | Not publicly enumerable. No names, fields or availability are invented. |

The source-only and declared-only appendices are included for discovery and compatibility analysis. They are not an instruction to enable experimental features, modify exporter destinations, or treat undocumented ingestion endpoints as stable APIs.

### compliance_event_type_response

Values: `APP_AUTH_LOG`, `APP_LOG`, `AUDIT_LOG`, `CONVERSATION_MESSAGE`, `COSTS`, `etc...`.

Type: `string`.

| Field | Type | Presence | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |


## Full workspace audit-action identifier catalog

Each row is an `AUDIT_LOG.action` identifier from the public schema, including old compatibility actions still documented. The action name says what operation was recorded; `action_result` establishes success/block/error. The last column retains native field and allowed-value tokens from the action description; it is not a list of universally required top-level keys. This does not authorize performing any action listed here. Some RBAC activity has moved to the API Platform audit surface; both contracts must be consulted during migration.

| Action | Recorded operation | Native field / value tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WORKSPACE_CODEX_REPOSITORY_REVIEW_UPDATE` | workspace codex repository review update | `fields`, `mutation_applied`, `repository`, `review_preference`, `security_review.severity_threshold` |

## Completeness, provenance and evidence limits

This document is exhaustive over the collected catalogs listed below, with source-defined runtime names reconciled against the literal census. It is not a claim to enumerate OpenAI’s private backend metrics or every future dynamic event. No public, immutable full telemetry schema exists for the continuously deployed ChatGPT/cloud backend. Missing proprietary fields are explicitly unknown, not silently treated as absent. A source declaration is not a delivery test.

| Catalog | Entries included |
| --- | --- |
| Named runtime events | 46 |
| Runtime metrics | 256 |
| Source span names | 236 |
| CLI internal analytics event types | 35 |
| Serialized analytics payload structures | 72 |
| Analytics and referenced protocol enums | 55 |
| Desktop literal metric scope/name pairs | 202 |
| Desktop protobuf analytics type declarations | 1118 |
| Desktop descriptor call sites | 1722 |
| Desktop types referenced by call sites | 1015 |
| Desktop type/field pairs visible at call sites | 4014 |
| Public audit action identifiers | 295 |
| Public authentication actions | 13 |
| Public analytics/metadata response schemas | 36 |
| Documentation-only metric discrepancies | 8 |

Source-census exclusions were executable/socket filenames, configuration selectors, test filenames and protobuf package/service names. Inbound metadata and attribute-only strings were classified separately. These exclusions prevent a substring search from falsely presenting every `codex.*` string as telemetry.

| Excluded literal | Why it is not an event/metric |
| --- | --- |
| `codex.accent` | Terminal color/theme identifier. |
| `codex.app` | Application bundle name. |
| `codex.code_mode.v1` | Protobuf package name. |
| `codex.exe` | Executable filename. |
| `codex.sock` | Socket filename. |
| `codex.thread_config.v1.ThreadConfigLoader` | gRPC service name. |
| `exec_server_args_tests.rs` | Test filename. |
| `exec_server_auth_tests.rs` | Test filename. |
| `exec_server_remote` | Feature/configuration identifier. |
| `exec_server_strict_config` | Configuration identifier. |
| `exec_server_telemetry_tests.rs` | Test filename. |
| `exec_server_url` | Configuration identifier. |

```json
              "tool_namespace": "%tool_namespace",
              "tool_result_seq": "tool_result_seq"
            },
            "log": {
              "agent_name": "%telemetry.metadata.agent_name",
              "arguments": "%arguments",
              "mcp_server": "%mcp_server",
              "mcp_server_origin": "%mcp_server_origin",
              "output": "%preview.text"
            },
            "trace": {
              "arguments_length": "arguments.len() as i64",
              "mcp_tool": "!mcp_server.is_empty()",
              "output_length": "output.len() as i64",
              "output_line_count": "output.lines().count() as i64",
              "tool_origin": "if mcp_server.is_empty() { \"builtin\" } else { \"mcp\" }"
            }
          },
          "target": []
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```
